_what: Transitions, grips and the size key, after Matt's play-test.

grips.stills: GRIPS.jpg -- the right fist closed on the haft reads clearly at the strike; the idle framings are obstructed by the mantle and the shield, which is a framing limit of shooting a hand inside a kitted figure, not a grip that failed.

idle_scale_bug.verdict: the corrected GLB is bound: the idle carries NO Hips scale track, and the shoulder span and head length are identical across idle, walk and run to four decimals (+0.00%). Screen silhouette height was NOT used for this, per the note that fore-aft extent projects 0.798 screen-metres per metre against stature's 0.603.

size_key.defaults: 1.00 in lit mode, 1.10 in painted, until Matt picks
size_key.note: canvas px are measured head_end-to-feet in the IDLE pose, which stands with bent knees -- a perfectly straight 1.85 m figure would read 112 px at scale 1.0. These numbers are also 15% below the ones reported before the idle fix, which is the 17.6% Hips scale coming out.

A_B_one_instrument._why: the 10.2 mm / 219 mm figures recorded for the pre-sync build were taken with an instrument that counted airborne frames and tested only one end of each pair, so they cannot be compared with these. --no-sync restores the pre-sync behaviour so ONE instrument measures both.

sync_group._what: The walk<->run crossover slide, done at runtime as a normalized-phase sync group: AnimationNodeTimeScale on each locomotion child playing at len_clip/len_blended, run phase offset so its left-foot contact lands on the walk's. No asset change.
sync_group.phase_align_only_while_weightless: seeking a branch that is contributing to the pose teleports it -- 1.09 m in one frame, measured.
sync_group.run_weight: solved by bisection on the blended foot speed, not read linearly off speed: S(w) = lerp(stride_w, stride_r, w) / lerp(len_w, len_r, w), which is NOT lerp(speed_w, speed_r, w). Reading it linearly is what the BlendSpace1D did and it is why equal cycle times made the slide worse.

tau_sweep_worst_mm._cols: [run-stop worst, crossover worst]; 0.20 is the lowest joint

the_floor_the_CLIPS_impose._how: each clip alone, at its authored rate, body advanced at exactly that clip's own stride-derived speed. No blending, no sync group. Whatever remains is the clip's and no runtime blend can go below it.

two_instrument_defects_fixed_on_the_way: AIRBORNE FRAMES COUNTED. Walking him in one direction for 86 frames at up to 6.4 m/s takes him off the plateau. The body was travelling 0.569 m per frame where its speed says 0.084 -- a fall -- and the 'planted' foot was falling with it. Every spike over 0.25 m in the first run of this, including a 1.12 m frame, was that. Fixed: require is_on_floor(), and drive him out and back so he stays on the plateau.

ONLY ONE END OF EACH PAIR TESTED. At 6.4 m/s the foot that lands on frame N was 0.4 m behind and airborne on N-1, so its 'travel' is the swing, measured correctly, and is not a slide. Fixed: both frames of the pair must be in contact, and the foot's height must not change between them, because the ground does not move.
sync_group.verdict: TARGET PARTLY MET. The 219 mm frame is gone: the worst frame anywhere in the test is 119.6 mm, down 45% from the pre-sync build's 218.5 mm, and it is in the RUN STOP -- not the crossover, which is where my previous commit attributed it. The crossover is the sync group's clear win: sync off gives ONE grounded-at-both-ends pair in 84 frames (142.3 mm), sync on gives 13, worst 104.7 mm. The 2.9 mm median target CANNOT be reached at run speed and the reason is the asset, which was excluded from scope: the run clip alone, nothing blended, never produces a stance pair under 15.4 mm and has ZERO pairs under 10 mm in a full cycle. 2.9 mm is a walk-speed number -- the walk is 24 frames per cycle at 2.0 m/s, the run is 15 frames at 6.4 m/s, so 4.3x the foot speed sampled at 0.6x the frames. Closing it needs the run re-timed to a whole multiple of the walk's cycle, or captured at more frames.
sync_group.what_the_height_band_still_cannot_do: floor_y taken over a leg that spans two gaits is anchored to the run's deepest compression (0.015 m above the root) and so admits the run's lifting foot while rejecting the settled idle's genuinely flat feet (0.046-0.061 m). The 119.6 mm worst pair passes every filter and is a foot SKIMMING into contact at 6.4 m/s, which a 24 fps sample cannot distinguish from a plant.

t9_1c_parked.state: the relief is built and in the scene behind --no-relief; the depth-residual sweep was cut when the character work was re-prioritised.
t9_1c_parked.the_finding: IT DOES NOT MOVE THE LIGHTING. near-black 19.04% -> 18.93%, lost>half 16.20% -> 16.08%. Switching shadows off changes nothing (15.27% -> 15.25%) and doubling the sun changes nothing (15.02%), so the dark is not shadow and not intensity. With NO sun and full ambient -- the painted albedo shown flat -- 10.54% of the frame is STILL near-black: over half the darkness is painted into the plate. 1b, the albedo repaint, is the load-bearing step, not 1c.
t9_1c_parked.what_was_measured: the displacement is along the VIEW direction, so the painted registration is exact: the tree frame is pixel-identical before and after (0 of 2,073,600 px differ), the bridge frame differs on 0.58% purely from depth reordering at the chasm lip. Near wall: 10,324 of 37,810 vertices moved, mean 0.445 m, max 2.5 m.

transitions.brief_was: 0.25-0.35 s from a walk, 0.4-0.5 s from a run
transitions.how: locomotion is an AnimationNodeBlendSpace1D on GROUND SPEED (idle 0 / walk 201.7 / run 647.5 canvas px/s), sync on; the attack is an AnimationNodeOneShot over the top (0.10 s in, 0.25 s out); the facing turn is an exponential lerp on the yaw. There is no state switch left in the locomotion, which is what the snap was.
transitions.one_speed_drives_both: the smoothed speed positions the blend AND moves the body. If either smoothed and the other did not, the feet would slide for exactly as long as the ramp lasted.
transitions.slide_note: a planted foot is one that does not move, because the ground does not. So the test is the stance foot's travel IN WORLD SPACE while planted -- filtered to frames where it is within 3 cm of its own lowest, because at a run the SWINGING foot can be the lower of the two for a frame and travels 0.22 m in it, correctly. The walk stop is 2.9 mm per frame, which is 7 cm/s against a body doing 2 m/s. The run stop is 10.2 mm median with one frame at 219 mm at the walk-run crossover: that single frame is the phase mismatch between a 25-frame walk and a 16-frame run. Godot's blend-space `sync` keeps both clips running but cannot time-lock clips of different length. The asset fix is to re-time the run to a whole multiple of the walk's cycle; shortening the ramp already took the median from 61 mm to 10 mm.
